goal: Search for bath towels and return the prices of the top 3 cheapest ones available

steps.rationale: Amazon shows a 'continue shopping' interstitial before the storefront; clicking it is required to reach the search box.
The main site search box is the entry point for the product query; typing the search term here is the reusable parameter of this capability.
Submitting with the 'Go' button uses the exact typed query rather than a hardcoded autocomplete suggestion, so replay works for any search term.

Sorting ascending by price makes the first three result rows the three cheapest by construction, instead of scanning and comparing 48 featured prices — this is what makes the extraction reliable on replay.
The results list is not yet in the accessibility tree; the built-in 'Skip to main search results' link moves focus into the results region, which should load/expose the product rows.

blockedReason: The navigation half of this capability records cleanly: search "bath towels" from the storefront search box, then set the "Sort by" combobox to "Price: Low to High" so the first three result rows are by construction the three cheapest. What cannot be recorded is the output. Every price node fails extract() with "no anchor; its value cannot be relocated on a fresh page" — I tried (1) the price links in the results grid, (2) the bare price text immediately following the "Price, product page" label in a result row, and (3) the buy-box price on the product detail page (/dp/B0F93YTRV4), adjacent to "In Stock". On these screens only spec-table cells are anchored to stable labels (e.g. "Gray"->Color, "Generic"->Brand, "Cotton"->Material); prices are unanchored positional text. For a human's reference, today's sorted-ascending top three read $0.02 (2 Pack Microfiber Towel Set, In Stock), $0.69 (Soft Cotton Bath Towel Set) and $0.98 (Bath Towels, 3 Pack Coral Fleece) — but I am deliberately not committing these via extract(), because a recorded step that cannot relocate its target would either fail on replay or bind to whatever text occupies that grid position next time, silently returning a wrong price. Note also that the cheapest listings here are sub-$1 items with $7.99-$12.99 shipping, so "cheapest by item price" may not be the intended business meaning of cheapest. — blocked on: Need a price element that the extractor can anchor to a stable label. Options a human could decide on: expose the existing "Price, product page" label as a real anchor for the adjacent price text in each result row; or point me at a screen where price is rendered in a labelled row (e.g. an order-detail or item-details table with a "Price:" label) that I can drive to per product; or confirm that unanchored, position-based price extraction is acceptable for replay and I will re-record it with that caveat. Also please confirm whether "cheapest" should rank on item price or item price plus shipping.
